metadata.title_guess: Interfacial Control of Resistive Switching in Ti/Au–Si Memristive Junctions

evidence_registry.text: The Ti/Au–Si junctions switch from a high-resistance state of 1.2 × 10^5 Ω to a low-resistance state of 9.8 × 10^2 Ω after electroforming at 2.8 ± 0.2 V.
The ON/OFF ratio remained above 10^2 for 10^4 s at 85 °C under a 0.1 V read bias.
The current–voltage curves between 300 and 400 K are consistent with Poole–Frenkel emission from interfacial traps.
The extracted activation energy is 0.18 ± 0.02 eV, and the trap density is estimated as 2.4 × 10^18 cm^-3.
Devices endured 500 write–erase cycles without a decline larger than 12% in the ON/OFF ratio.
Cross-sectional TEM confirmed a continuous 3.5 nm TiOx layer between Si and the Ti/Au contact.
The set voltage scales with the square root of the electric field, as expected for trap-assisted conduction.
The study is limited to n-type Si substrates and 100 µm junctions; CMOS integration and high-frequency operation were not tested.
The conduction fit cannot uniquely separate Poole–Frenkel emission from Schottky emission, and the trap density is an order-of-magnitude estimate.
